findings.title: Rendering a DOCX with a renamed numbering part can exhaust the process stack
findings.summary: A document author can point the internal numbering relationship at deeply nested XML named `numbering.bin`. Admission skips XML depth and tag policy for that auxiliary filename, but the renderer parses it recursively, allowing a compact DOCX to terminate the conversion process.

severity.rationale: Attacker-controlled document data deterministically bypasses the depth policy and can abort a local conversion or an embedding worker. Exposure is constrained to a caller choosing to process that document; no remote service or cross-tenant deployment is established, and SECURITY.md recommends process CPU/memory limits.
severity.changeConditions: A shared service accepting public document uploads without per-job process isolation would increase operational impact; enforcing XML limits at each semantic consumer removes this path.

confidence.rationale: Static trace connects the extension-based admission decision, relationship-selected numbering part and unchecked recursive parser. No runtime trigger was executed.

codeEvidence.label: Render entry admits package
codeEvidence.explanation: Caller-controlled DOCX bytes are admitted before the same bytes are normalized and opened.

codeEvidence.label: Admission chooses XML by extension
codeEvidence.explanation: Only .xml and .rels entries receive XML policy checks; a numbering.bin entry is treated as binary.

codeEvidence.label: Only the main part has an extension exception
codeEvidence.explanation: The extra check for non-XML names applies to the main document, leaving auxiliary relationship targets unchecked.

codeEvidence.label: Numbering relationship controls the selected part
codeEvidence.explanation: The document's internal numbering relationship selects an arbitrary package part, excluding external targets but imposing no XML policy.

codeEvidence.label: Selected numbering bytes reach permissive parsing
codeEvidence.explanation: The selected part is decoded as text and passed to the recursive DOM parser without checked parsing.

codeEvidence.label: DOM recursion has no depth argument
codeEvidence.explanation: Each nested element recursively invokes parse_element; the skipped admission depth bound is the only protection on this path.

rootCause.summary: `admit()` classifies XML by filename and only adds a nonstandard-extension exception for the main part. `main_rel_part()` trusts internal relationship targets, so `load_numbering()` can select an auxiliary `.bin` part. `parse_numbering_xml()` invokes the permissive DOM parser, whose element recursion has no depth limit, without validating the selected bytes.

findings.remediation: Apply the active XML depth/tag limits to every relationship-selected part immediately before DOM parsing, regardless of filename, and use bounded or iterative parsing as defense in depth.

limitations: No malicious file was generated or executed.
Other XML consumers were not exhaustively enumerated; this finding establishes the numbering path.
validation.summary: Verified that `with_layout()` admits input, `admit()` omits XML checks on non-.xml/.rels auxiliary entries, `main_rel_part()` selects the attacker-controlled internal target, and `load_numbering()` parses it without a second check. PartFs inflation caps and strict translation constrain bytes but do not validate the auxiliary XML nesting.

dataflow.summary: DOCX bytes -> admission extension filter -> internal numbering relationship -> part_string -> parse_numbering_xml -> recursive parse_element
dataflow.source: attacker-controlled package relationship and auxiliary part bytes

impact.why: A stack overflow aborts the processing worker.

likelihood.why: Requires the victim to process attacker-provided DOCX; no public deployment is assumed.

limitations: Process isolation contains the failure to the selected job.

reachability.summary: Any caller processing a document supplied by a lower-trust author through the public render API can reach this path; neither external relationship fetching nor filesystem access is required.
reachability.entrypoint: convert::docx_to_pdf and the shared layout pipeline

attackPath.summary: Supply a valid DOCX whose numbering relationship targets a `.bin` entry containing deeply nested elements, then call `docx_to_pdf()` or another renderer using the shared layout pipeline.

remediationTests: Render a DOCX with a deeply nested `numbering.bin` relationship target and assert an INVALID_XML refusal before DOM construction.
Retain support for nonstandard auxiliary filenames within the configured XML limits.

originalCandidates.title: Non-XML numbering relationship target bypasses admission depth checking
originalCandidates.originalWorkerMessage: Static audit has identified two concrete DoS paths for final JSON: admission only depth-checks .xml/.rels plus main, while render resolves numbering relationship to arbitrary extension and recursively parses it unchecked; and unescape_xml_text scans the remaining suffix at each '&', with raw ampersand text passing admission. Continuing counterevidence and exact locations; no application code executed.
originalCandidates.originalEvidence: src/admission.rs:534 defines is_xml = lower.ends_with(".xml") || lower.ends_with(".rels"), calls check_xml_depth only inside that branch at 543; only special exception at 555-569 is main part. src/convert/mod.rs:6557-6570 load_numbering calls main_rel_part(pkg,"numbering",...) then part_string then dom.parse_xdocument(xml); main_rel_part at 21310-21322 uses relationship target without extension restriction. Parser recursively calls self.parse_element(scope) at src/xmllinq/parse.rs:660-661, no local depth limit. An internal numbering relationship Target='numbering.bin' with 100k nested <x> elements survives ZIP byte/depth admission and stack-overflows rendering.

candidate.title: Repeated ampersands induce quadratic unescape scanning
candidate.originalWorkerMessage: unescape_xml_text scans the remaining suffix at each '&', with raw ampersand text passing admission.
candidate.originalEvidence: src/xmllinq/parse.rs:766-794 unescape_xml_text, at each '&' finds ';' by scanning chars[i+1..].iter().position, and advances only 1 when no valid entity. Text containing '&'.repeat(N) passes check_xml_depth (src/admission.rs:806-842 ignores Event::Text) and each parse_element text call invokes unescape_xml_text at parse.rs:668-670. O(N^2) CPU with a tiny compressed main XML.
candidate.counterevidence: No dependency source inside target establishes whether quick-xml 0.42 accepts raw ampersands without a semicolon. Baseline suggests terminated malformed reference or arbitrary-extension part; arbitrary-extension route avoids the scanner, while the direct public unescape_xml_text API also accepts caller-controlled strings. Main-part reachability remains unverified.

candidate.originalEvidence: Story::blocks at legacy_doc.rs:1605 computes fields.iter().any for every character, field begin pushes true, separator sets last false. Input repeating '\x13\x14' N times creates N false field levels; every subsequent pair scans all prior false levels. O(N²) on ~2N text bytes, no nesting/depth limit. read() and CLI convert reach it directly; separate from XML parser.
